notes: Native-rate campaign, 18-20 Sep 2026, RunPod RTX PRO 6000, CARLA 0.9.15 Epic. Driven at 10 Hz, set with PADDOCK_INFER_HZ; alpamayo15/model.yaml declares native_input_hz 10.0, which agrees. routes_file, routes_subset and waypoint_dt are identical to the 20 Hz pooled50 run; that run also set ALPAMAYO_NAV=1, ALPAMAYO_RESERVE_GB=0 and MKL/OMP_NUM_THREADS=2, and this one set none of them -- ALPAMAYO_NAV defaults to 1 in policy.py, so both campaigns ran with the nav instruction on. The simulator build and the shared tracker and controller were the same, and are recorded in neither run. Route 3800 (Town13 MergerIntoSlowTraffic) left no scoring checkpoint at this rate: two attempts, 20260919T004052-2ce451 stopping after infer #601 and 20260919T062659-2ce451 after infer #701, about 1200 and 1400 sim frames. Neither wrote an evaluator log, so the CARLA Signal=11 is recorded for qwendrive on this route and not for this model; the node logs are the evidence here. DriveJEPA completes the same route at 2 Hz and scores 100, and this model scored it 35.33 at 20 Hz, so the failure follows the rate under test rather than the route. 49 of 49 source runs kept no run.json, so their routes are attributed to alpamayo15 on the tree they were found in; config.model_env and the rest of config are what 49/49 source runs recorded. PADDOCK_INFER_HZ was supplied by the ingest config and recorded by no source run, so it is the operator's assertion about the campaign, not a reading from it. driven at 10 Hz, not the 20 Hz the benchmark's published protocol calls the model at. paddock ingest wrote this run valid: false; it was marked valid on 29 Oct 2026, so the support matrix and the leaderboard rank the model at its native rate. Its mean is over the 49 routes that scored: route 3800 is named at the end of this note as never scored, not counted as a zero. The paired 20 Hz comparison is docs/benchmarks/bench2drive-native-rate.md. routes expected but never scored: 3800 (no attempt found).
